posts.name: Diffracted
posts.cooked:
As someone in the tech space, it’s likely to affect WoW in some way. How much and where is the question.

Most companies will not tell you. They instead cut workers, trim timelines, and in general push doing more with less.

You’ve already seen the effects of this attitude (do more with less) for years with customer service. First companies sent it abroad. They reduced options for repair. Then, they used various automation technologies for templates. GenAI is likely handling front line tickets in some way as the next escalation of templates (if you @ me on this, folks, I spent years deploying these exact solutions).

They’ve been open that they are using it for armor fitting. Look at research coming from Blizz or publications from their research department. That gives you some clue to what they’re testing.

Anyone in development is likely using a level of AI augmented code. Prior, it was some things like Stack Overflow or internal repos of code snippets. It’s also one of the ways they’re likely testing code in some way.

Decor may likely use a level of AI in reskinning, potential idea formation (scan existing assets and see what can be converted to the decor model), and fitting into whatever changes are required to take a previously passive developer asset into a player usable one.

If you’re looking for actions to protest, they tend to be the wildly unsatisfying ones: not purchasing RMT, unsubs, etc. Yes, you can post, but the broader ecosystem of tech does not care. They are hard shoving AI augmentation.

posts.name: Evilsmurf
posts.cooked:
Cörëdûmp:

erasure-coded, multi-site storage

Iron Mountain still has clients who do use tapes. Some companies have switch to a mix of cloud and tape.

Instead of daily backups they move to weekly etc.

And when you have a large company with many sites and huge amount of data erasure-coded multi-site storage isnt going to come close to beating the speed and convenience of backup tapes. Nor do backup tapes clog the bandwidth of people actually trying to do work.

posts.name: mizzou
posts.cooked: I used to be a SAN/storage architect at a large Fortune 10 company. I had 8 Sun Sl8500 tape silo’s with 8 robots each. I am sooooooooooooooo glad tape is dying. I’ve put my hands on more backup tapes than I care to remember. We used to vault an entire 26-foot Iron Mountain truck full of tapes offsite twice a week. And special source code backups were literally flown to Reston, VA and stored in a 150ft undeground vault.
